This application coming on for hearing this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER They are heard.
Perused the case diary / challan papers.

This is applicant's first application under Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail, as the present applicant is apprehending his / her arrest in connection with Crime No.30/2023 registered at Police Station Kantafod, District Dewas (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 409 & 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegation against the applicant is of defalcation of a sum of Rs.88,48,112/-, as it is alleged that the applicant purchased the food grains of the complainant on various dates.
However, despite selling the same onwards, the amount was not paid to the Vendors.
Counsel for the applicant has submitted the applicant has already paid a sum of around Rs.12,00,000/- to the complainant, which shows that his intention was not to cheat the complainant.

It is further submitted that the applicant had already written a police complaint to the concerned police station on 21.5.2022 that his partner is misusing the Firm's account and is responsible for the defalcation and only thereafter the FIR was lodged and, hence, the application for anticipatory bail be allowed.

Counsel appearing for the respondent/State as also for the objector have opposed the prayer and it is submitted that a meagre amount has been paid to the Vendors initially and after gaining their confidence, the applicant obtained a huge quantity of food grains to the tune of Rs.88,48,112/- and has failed to pay back to the Vendors the consideration of the food grains.
Thus, it is apparent that right from the beginning, the applicant had an intention to cheat the complainant party and despite being a Merchant, he has committed the aforesaid offence.
Thus, it is submitted that no case for grant of anticipatory bail is made out as the offence clearly falls u/s.409 of IPC.

On due consideration of the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary as also the documents placed on record by the counsel for the applicant, this Court finds force in the submissions as advanced by the counsel for the respondent/State and the Objector and is of the considered opinion that in the present case, the intention of the applicant to cheat from the beginning is apparent from the face on record, and hence, the custodial interrogation of the applicant would be necessary.
Accordingly, the M.Cr.C. being devoid of merits, is hereby dismissed.
